paras: The killing of Thomas Phearby took place on September 1, 1882, when Officer John Foster shot Phearby, a Black prisoner in his charge, in the woods about four miles from Spartanburg, South Carolina. A coroner's jury found that Phearby died from a pistol ball fired by Foster, and Foster was jailed.

Phearby had been committed to the Spartanburg County jail for thirty days on a charge of disturbing religious worship in the upper part of the county. Foster had him "in charge" on September 1, apparently bringing him toward the city.

According to the Spartanburg correspondent, Phearby "sprang into the woods" four miles from the city and was soon hidden by the undergrowth. Foster fired a small .32-calibre pistol in his direction and, in the dispatch's words, "was astonished to hear groans" and to find his prisoner lying forty-five yards away. The ball entered the back of Phearby's head, and he died soon afterward. The dispatch names no witness to the flight or the shot, and no other version of the shooting was found.

Late that night a coroner's jury, after hearing a recital of these facts, returned the verdict "Death from a pistol ball fired by John Foster." Foster was then held in jail "awaiting the due course of the law." No report of an indictment or trial appears in the coverage found.

The only report found is a brief dated Spartanburg, September 2, credited to a correspondent of the Columbia Register and reprinted on September 8 in the Weekly Union Times of Union, South Carolina. It ran under the headline "Negro Killed by a Random Shot," a phrase that cast the killing as an accident, while the body of the item reported the jury's finding against Foster and his jailing without comment.
